summary: Norway Bluff 24-ft steel lookout (Piscataquis Co., ME) had a watchman's camp and phone line by 1914; removed May 2012, restored and exhibited at the Ashland Logging Museum.

facts.design: 24-foot steel lookout tower (1914 Forest Commissioner's report; 1920 inventory)
facts.status_note: The original Norway Bluff site is listed as gone; the tower stands as an exhibit at the Ashland Logging Museum (FFLA lists it as standing there).

events.note: Built during the summer before the 1914 Forest Commissioner's report (exact year not stated)
Watchman's camp built on the mountainside; telephone line gave the lookout man a connection to Oxbow Plantation
Chief fire warden J.E. Junkins reported trees cleared off the bluff so the country could be seen without climbing the tower
Taken off the mountain on 7 May 2012 for the MSCommNet radio project; the Maine Forest Service dismantled the tower
Moved to the Ashland Logging Museum on 13 June 2012
Volunteers and Ashland Boy Scout Troop 179 put in well over 600 hours on the cab, painted frame and reassembly
Dedication ceremony held at the Ashland Logging Museum on 7 July 2013

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts gives only 'May 2012' for the dismantling. The 2012 FFLA report gives 7 May 2012 for removal from the mountain and 13 June 2012 for arrival at the museum. These agree; the story uses the report's dates.

notes_for_editor: The destination record (us-me-norway-bluff-at-ashland-logging-museum) gives a 'wood cab, reconditioned for the move' design. None of the pages read for this story states the cab material, so the story does not repeat it. The 1914 report gives no exact build year; the event note says so. The museum's visiting arrangements are not described in the pages read, so the story asks visitors to check with the museum.
